checks.public_requirement: Exactly one output file named ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv is delivered as the only content of the submission directory (it may instead sit alone inside an empty subdirectory named 'outputs' or 'output'). The file is non-empty UTF-8 text with no byte-order mark, comma-delimited, with exactly one header line reading chrom,start,end,fc,motif_chrom,motif_start,motif_end,motif_pval,motif_strand, followed by at least one data row of exactly nine fields, with no blank lines (a final newline is expected; CRLF is read as a newline).

Every data row carries: a non-empty chrom (no whitespace or commas); start and end as plain non-negative integers with start < end; fc as a finite decimal number (blank, non-numeric, NaN or infinite values fail); and a motif block that is either blank in all five fields (motif_chrom, motif_start, motif_end, motif_pval, motif_strand) or complete in all five, with motif_start and motif_end plain non-negative integers satisfying motif_start < motif_end, a finite decimal motif_pval, a motif_strand that is exactly '+' or '-', and motif_chrom identical to the row's chrom. A partially specified motif block fails.

Grouping rows by their (chrom, start, end) triple, the set of retained peak sub-intervals equals the reference set exactly: every reference interval is reported at least once, no interval outside the reference set is reported, and no row is an exact duplicate of another row (identical in all nine fields). Peaks split into several retained sub-intervals contribute one row per surviving sub-interval; peaks entirely removed by the blacklist contribute no row. Row order is not evaluated.

Grouping rows by (chrom, start, end), every reference (interval, fc) pair is reported by at least one row of the submission, with fc compared as the exact parsed decimal number (only the rendering of an equal value is normalized). A missing interval, an altered or rounded fc value, or an unparseable / NaN / infinite fc fails this check. Reporting additional fc values for an interval that corresponds to more than one peak record in the input is not penalized by this check.

Grouping rows by (chrom, start, end), all rows sharing an interval must carry the same motif block, and that block must equal the reference motif assignment for the interval: either blank in all five fields (peak with no assigned motif), or motif_chrom = chrom, and motif_start, motif_end, motif_strand identical to the reference with motif_pval equal as the exact parsed decimal number. Any interval whose reported block is blank where the reference has a motif, non-blank where the reference has none, or disagrees in any motif field fails.

instruction:
# Acceptance rules (addendum to the task specification)

## Output file and format

Write **exactly one** output file, `ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv`, and nothing else. It must be the only content of your submission directory (a tolerated variant: the file sitting alone inside an otherwise-empty subdirectory named exactly `outputs` or `output`). No logs, indices or sidecar files. The file is UTF-8, comma-separated, with exactly one header line and one data row per retained peak sub-interval, no index column and no additional columns. Lines must end with a newline; blank lines anywhere (including the last line) fail. A final newline is expected; CRLF line endings are read as newlines. A gzipped output fails.

The header line must read exactly:

```
chrom,start,end,fc,motif_chrom,motif_start,motif_end,motif_pval,motif_strand
```

Each data row has exactly nine comma-separated fields in that order. Tab-, semicolon- or space-delimited files fail, as does a byte-order mark or any non-UTF-8 byte sequence.

## Field value rules

- `chrom`, `motif_chrom` — contig name (e.g. `chr1`), matched by exact string. Blank or malformed values fail.
- `start`, `end`, `motif_start`, `motif_end` — plain non-negative base-pair integers, compared numerically and exactly. Leading `+`, leading zeros, non-integer renderings (`48309541.0`, `4.8e7`) and negative values all fail.
- `start < end` and `motif_start < motif_end` must hold in every row.
- `fc` — the peak's fold change, a finite decimal number. Renderings that parse to the same number are accepted (`5.208`, `5.20800`, `5.208e0`); blank, non-numeric, `NaN` or infinite values fail. All rows belonging to one peak (including split sub-intervals) carry that peak's fold change.
- `motif_pval` — −log10(p) × 100, a finite decimal number, admitted under the same rendering rule.
- `motif_strand` — exactly `+` or `-`.
- **A blank motif block is an answer, not missing data.** A peak with no assigned motif must have all five motif fields blank. A partially blank block (e.g. motif coordinates present but motif_pval blank) fails: it is neither a valid assignment nor a valid "no motif" answer. Such rows are never treated as missing or dropped values, and `NaN`/infinite values in numeric fields always fail rather than comparing equal.
- Every row's `motif_chrom` equals its `chrom`.

## Row alignment, ordering and multiplicity

Rows are aligned to the reference by the stable identifier `(chrom, start, end)` of the retained peak sub-interval. **Row order is free and is not compared.**

- The set of distinct `(chrom, start, end)` intervals in the submission must equal the reference set exactly: no reference interval may be absent, and no interval outside the reference may appear. One row is emitted per retained peak sub-interval; a peak split into several pieces contributes one row per piece with the same annotations; a peak entirely removed by the expanded blacklist contributes no row. Peaks that appear more than once in the peak file may be reported in one row or in several rows for the same interval (see fold-change rule below).
- No row may be an exact duplicate of another row (identical in all nine fields). Every distinct row must be reported once.

## What is compared scientifically

The submission is compared against the reference copy of this table, which was produced by the approved analysis: strongest-overlapping-motif assignment on the original, untrimmed peak spans, followed by ±1 kb expanded-blacklist trimming of the reported coordinates. Comparison is per interval, after alignment by `(chrom, start, end)`. Three quantities are checked as separate named checks, so a submission that gets the intervals right but the annotation wrong (or the reverse) fails on the corresponding check:

1. **Retained peak sub-intervals** — which peaks survived where, i.e. the trimmed coordinates (set equality as above).
2. **Peak fold change** — for every reference `(interval, fc)` pair, at least one row of the submission for that interval must report that fc. Comparison is by the exact parsed number with **no tolerance**: any difference, including one unit in the last digit, fails. Only the decimal rendering of an equal number is normalized away. Where an interval belongs to more than one peak record, rows reporting the additional records' fold changes are not penalized by this check, but the reference value must be present and every reported value must be attached to a reference interval.
3. **Motif assignment** — for every reference interval, all submission rows for that interval must carry the same motif block, equal to the reference assignment: either blank in all five fields, or the reference `motif_chrom`, `motif_start`, `motif_end`, `motif_strand` exactly and `motif_pval` equal as the exact parsed number. Turning a blank block into a motif, dropping a motif, swapping motifs between peaks, changing the strand, or changing the score by any amount fails.

The assigned motif is not required to overlap the reported, possibly trimmed sub-interval (assignment uses the original untrimmed peak span, as specified), and this overlap is not checked. The grader does not re-run the analysis and does not read the raw inputs; it evaluates the delivered table only.

## Failure handling

A missing output file, unreadable file, malformed CSV, wrong header, wrong column count, blank lines, non-numeric or nonfinite numeric field, partially blank motif block, or a motif on a chromosome other than the peak's own fails the corresponding checks. All declared checks are reported in every case; a failure upstream of a check makes that check fail (it is reported as not evaluated), never a crash. The grader exits 0 with a written report for both correct and incorrect submissions.
rationale:
SCOPE. One endpoint, outputs/ctcf_peaks_maxmotif_clean.csv, graded on parsed scientific content against the reference copy of that file (40557 data rows; the reference export's chrom_2/start_2/end_2/pval_2/strand_2 columns were renamed to the public schema by the recorded, hash-verified derive script; values and rows unchanged).

EVIDENCE (recorded executions only; I re-parsed files, I did not rerun the analysis): reference export d513065e...; independent re-execution of the reference pipeline (/work/recomputed, byte-identical, all_outputs_byte_identical_to_original); separately executed independent solution (/work/alternative, no answer access) that the controller requires to PASS.

CONTROL-DRIVEN CHANGE (first submission was rejected on exactly this point): the controller ran my first candidate against /work/alternative and rejected it because I had required exact row-multiset equality over (chrom,start,end). The peaks file contains 15 intervals recorded twice with different fc (40587 rows, 40572 distinct intervals); the reference emits one row per distinct interval using the first record's fc, while the required-pass independent solution emits one row per peak record (40572 rows, carrying both fc values on those 15 intervals). Both are executions of the same scientific question, so per-record multiplicity is a documented freedom rather than a scientific error, and the fc rule is now reference-coverage over (interval, fc) pairs. Consequences I measured and then fenced off as far as the freedom allows: (i) a row identical to another in all nine fields still fails (padding probe passes rejected); (ii) replacing the reference fc with the second record's fc fails peak_fold_change (reference pair no longer covered); (iii) an interval reporting two different motif blocks fails motif_assignment (independent check), so the fc freedom cannot smuggle a wrong annotation; (iv) dropping an added extra row is not detectable by construction, and a fc value not present in the reference but attached to a reference interval is not rejected because the grader does not read the raw inputs — this is the honest boundary of the acceptance rule and it is stated in the public text.

NUMERIC RULES: for all 40557 shared rows, fc and motif_pval parsed from the two independently executed outputs are bit-identical (40557/40557 exact) while their string forms differ ("450" vs "450.0"; "5.208" vs "5.20800"). That is the observable signature of a deterministic exact-decimal analysis serialized by different writers, so fc and motif_pval are compared as parsed floats with no tolerance, and rendering normalization is confined to characters that parse to the same number. Coordinates and strand are compared exactly because they are the alignment identity. Blank-in-five-fields rows (5765 in the reference; both executions agree) are kept as first-class answers keyed by the all-blank motif block, so unannotated peaks cannot cancel a wrong table.

STRUCTURE: five checks — structural file/schema, structural field validity, and three scientific checks (retained intervals, fold change, motif assignment) keyed on (chrom,start,end) so trimming/multiplicity, fc and motif identity are independently discriminated. Measured discrimination on local probes: second-best motif, cross-peak motif swap, strand flip, pval -1, motif removal, blank-block fill, 1e-12/1e-6 fc perturbation, dropped/added/duplicated/trimmed/untrimmed rows, blacklisted-peak reintroduction, wrong header/order/index column, tab/semicolon delimiters, gz output, BOM, blank lines — all fail the intended check; shuffled/sorted/reversed order, scientific notation, padded decimals, CRLF, quoted fields pass. Runtime ~0.85 s and ~200 MB, far inside the 120 s verifier limit; the grader writes nothing into the reference or submission directories (hash-verified) and emits exactly {passed, checks[{id,passed,message}]}.

CSV parsing uses the stdlib csv module on one line at a time (next(csv.reader([line], strict=True))); a pathological header with an ambiguous number of fields is reported as a header mismatch rather than crashing. Reference-side load failures make the scientific checks fail with a clear message; the report and exit code 0 are still produced.

NOT DONE / ASSUMPTIONS: the extra-fc boundary in (iv) above is a deliberate, publicly stated freedom forced by the controller-required alternative; tightening it would reject a control that must pass. Harbor packaging, solver portability and the independent mutation suite are later stages. Disposition: ready.
